1.why: MFA routes require authenticated(session) with session.userId === ACCOUNT_ID, load records only via accountRecord(session), and reject client-supplied user/account identifiers through manipulated().

2.why: Identity OTPs are bound to the current session, TOTP is checked against that account’s draft/stored secret, and recovery codes live in the per-account mfaRecords entry—not shared across users.

3.why: POST /api/mfa/confirm enrols MFA and clears the draft but never deletes or rotates other existing sessions in the sessions Map, so prior sessions remain valid.

4.why: Authenticator secrets are stored with AES-GCM encryptAtRest, and recovery codes are stored only as salted SHA-256 digests, not plaintext.

5.why: Tokens, secrets, OTPs, and recovery codes are produced via crypto.getRandomValues through randomBytes/token/base32Secret/recoveryCode/randomDigits.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly; the SPA keeps csrf and secrets in memory only and never writes secrets/OTPs/tokens to localStorage, sessionStorage, or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server parsers email(), phone(), otp(), secret(), and recovery() enforce type/length/allow-list patterns before any auth or MFA logic uses the values.

8.why: Client rendering runs untrusted strings through escapeHTML, and responses are covered by a strict nonce-based CSP that blocks inline script injection.

9.why: No endpoint accepts a redirect target or emits Location-based redirects; navigation stays on same-origin API/UI paths only.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors DENY on responses.

11.why: sessionCookie() and clearCookie() set __Host-mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: API errors are generic with no stack traces; secrets are not written to server logs or URLs, and evaluation disclosures are console-only in non-production test mode.

13.why: Identity codes expire (IDENTITY_CODE_MS) and are cleared on success; enrolment drafts expire and are single-use; recovery codes are marked used after verification; TOTP is step-time-bound.

14.why: Identity, draft TOTP confirm, and recovery verify each increment failure counters and lock out for LOCK_MS after MAX_ATTEMPTS failures.

15.why: rotateSession() runs on sign-in and identity completion, getSession() enforces idle and absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
